newsitem.title: ITALY: Albanian refugee boat fires shots - report.
newsitem.headline: Albanian refugee boat fires shots - report.

text.p: Shots were fired from a fishing boat carrying Albanian refugees in the southern Adriatic on Monday as it was being towed by an Italian coastguard vessel, the Italian news agency ANSA reported.

The news agency quoted the commander of the coastguard in the southern port of Brindisi, Captain Giovanni Biso, as saying there were no injuries in the incident. Another coastguard official said he could not immediately confirm the report.
The official said coastguards were seeking more information on the incident from the captain of the patrol boat.
ANSA said shots were fired from the Albanian boat after the passengers realised the coastguard patrol vessel was towing them away from the port.
It quoted the captain of the patrol boat as saying he had received orders to "push the Albanians back where they came from".
The agency said that following the incident armed police and coastguards wearing bulletproof vests escorted the boat carrying around 100 Albanians into Brindisi.
They then boarded the fishing boat and one man was taken away by the police.
Brindisi is the main port of arrival for nearly 12,000 Albanian refugees who have reached Italy on a flotilla of rusty, old boats since March 13 to escape the chaos in their country.
